chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl bin Ziyad and Ahmad bin Muhammad, altogether, from Ibn Abi Nasr, who said: Hamza bin al-Yasa informed me, saying:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the leopard that was bought in Mina and taken out of the Haram. He said: 'Everything from the predatory wild animals that enters the Haram in captivity, you must take it out.'

key_terms.الْحَرَمِ: The Haram (the sacred precincts of Mecca)
key_terms.الْفَهْدِ: The leopard (a specific predatory wild animal)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on buying a wild animal in Mina and taking it into the Haram?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi clarifies the specific ruling for wild predatory beasts (al-sabu') brought into the Haram in captivity, establishing that they are considered 'ma'sur' (restrained) and must be removed to preserve the sanctity of the boundary. It highlights the juristic distinction between animals hunted within the Haram versus those merely transported into it, a key topic in Shia fiqh regarding the validity of hunting and associated expiations.
